feature: An animated picture exports as a GIF
summary: A picture with something moving on it now offers GIF on Export, and the file plays the same loop the timeline plays: round for ever, or once and holding where it landed when Repeat is off.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/a-moving-picture-exports-as-a-gif-walk.json.

try.do: On a still picture press Shift Command E. The format row has no GIF.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Draw a ball, press Add Key, drag it down, key it back at the top, press space to watch it bounce.
Press Shift Command E. GIF sits at the end of the format row, after SVG. Pick it.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Read the size line: a 512 ball is Animated GIF · 14 KB without its canvas, 33 KB with it.
Press Export… and open the file in Safari, Chrome and Preview.
Turn Repeat off on the keys bar, export again: the GIF bounces once and stays at the top.

evaluate: Is GIF where you looked for it, at the end of the format row?
Does the exported ball bounce at the same speed as it does on the canvas?
Is 14 to 33 KB for a 512 icon a size you would put in a README?
With Include the background off, are the GIF's hard edges acceptable, or should a GIF open with the background ticked?
rough: A GIF keeps a pixel either fully there or fully empty, so with the background left out the ball's edge is stepped rather than smooth. That is the format, not the export.
Bound for A README on a code host, the sheet picks PNG and says to record a video, which matches the mock icon-export-anim-wt.html.

The list of what survives now describes the format you picked, not only the destination's: GIF picked for a web page ticks the motion and crosses out Sharp at every size. Before, a PNG picked for a web page was said to keep its motion.
Frames are taken 25 a second (four hundredths each). A spinner on its own pace and a lap that only line up after more than 12 seconds export one lap long, with a small step at the seam.
The mock's sheet has no GIF button; it mentions a GIF only as the struck-out size beside the animated SVG. The app goes further than the mock here, as the task asked.
